description: Verify that DUT discards a truncated UDP datagram (wire region < 8 bytes — header itself is incomplete) (RFC 768 'Fields' MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
A UDP header is fixed at 8 bytes. If the L2/L3 wire delivers fewer than 8 bytes of UDP region, the header is incomplete and the datagram cannot be parsed. RFC 768 / RFC 1122 require the receiver to drop it.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 packet with UDP region < 8 bytes (e.g. 4 or 6 bytes)

2. Observation:
   • DUT's upper-tester must NOT receive the datagram (UT-query confirms drop)

[Pass condition]
UT-query confirms DUT did not deliver the truncated UDP.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_wrong_receipt — DUT delivered the truncated UDP (parser tolerated a sub-8-byte UDP region)
• Fail_timeout — UT-query never arrived (test infra issue)

verdicts.Pass: DUT discarded the sub-8-byte truncated UDP — normal
verdicts.Fail_wrong_receipt: DUT received a truncated sub-8-byte UDP
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No UT confirmation for truncated-UDP discard
